head: b6dd5ccd04b786cabe26804060f197b1f1daa3a8
classification_reasons: Spec is tight: every flagged concern is closed (panel #1, #2 and the owner's ratchet decision), and acceptance is measurable.

The blast radius is wide. Every app/data module is rewritten or deleted. The public frame contract loses three columns, along with BinanceBanError, the um market and the 1s interval. The cache moves to a new subtree. No risk-list item is touched and no stored data is migrated.

The paging and completeness logic (rest.py, loader.py) is new code, covered only by new tests against a new stub that encodes the measured KuCoin rules. The live endpoints are exercised only by the owner's deploy-gate downloads.
attempted: Scope of the test phase: the diff from the build gate's head (4ce80ac) to HEAD touches only changes/0003-.../evidence/ and status.yaml. No file under app/, tests/ or scripts/ changed after the build review, so I re-judged the whole change against origin/main.

Intent: the change loads KuCoin REST only from the two named hosts, with no key and one call at a time. vision.py, the zip and checksum handling and the thread pool are gone. Public names are kept; BinanceBanError is removed. Markets are spot and futures; 6h is refused on futures and 1s and um are refused. The frame has eight columns, close_time = open + interval - 1, and quote_volume comes from turnover. The contract-volume and short-frame notes are in the load_klines docstring and the download epilog, and the cache-clear epilog notes that old futures days may be lost. The cache subtree is kucoin/ and binance-vision/ is left untouched. The version stays 0.1.0. Every intent bullet is met.

Spec and plan: the diff's source files match plan.md 'Files that change'. The build departures are recorded in plan.md Risks: the test split plus conftest.py, _open_ms, an off-grid REST day settled as MISSING, the window-move guard, and the extra help test. Each Proof test name exists in tests/ (spot-checked in test_data_rest.py; the verifier did a full name comparison).

Paging correctness, spot (rest._fetch_spot): window_end starts at end_ms. Only rows with open < window_end move the window, so window_end = min(open) strictly decreases and the loop is bounded. A non-moving non-empty page is UNEXPECTED_RESPONSE with coverage [window_end, end). A refused page has the same coverage. An empty page ends the range as fully covered, which rests on the measured newest-kept rule (plan Risks).

Paging correctness, futures (rest._fetch_futures): to = end - 1. Rows at or after end_ms are dropped (the end-of-window row). window_start = max(open) + interval strictly increases. A failure leaves coverage [start, window_start).

Loader (loader._rest_pass / settle): a day is REST only when it lies fully in the covered span and has rows. A partly covered day is MISSING with the range's failure. An off-grid-only closed REST day becomes MISSING. _worth_caching is source == REST and today is never cached. A DownloadError is re-raised after the range's days are settled, so answered complete days stay cached (R22, panel #3).

Transport: with_retries resets retry_after on every attempt. A 429 without a usable Retry-After waits the gw-ratelimit-reset capped at 60 s; 60 is not above MAX_RETRY_AFTER, so it sleeps rather than raising. A 418 is returned. RateLimitPacer waits 1 s when either header is missing or not an integer, and waits the bounded reset when remaining < 100.

Untrusted input (security-baseline rule 2): the body size is bounded before json.loads, and ValueError and RecursionError are caught. The envelope must be a dict and code is compared as a string. msg and code are stripped to printable characters and cut, and a test checks escape-sequence stripping and the 200-character cut. Rows must have exactly 7 items with per-market types; bools are refused and futures float times must be integral. Times are bounded so close_time fits 64 bits, and prices must be finite. URLs are built with urlencode from validated symbols, against fixed https hosts.

Minor and not a reason: the spot time parser uses int(str), which also accepts '+', surrounding spaces and underscores. Any off-grid open time is then dropped by _on_grid. The worst case is a closed day cached with fewer rows from a malformed but code-200000 answer. That is the accepted loss of integrity checking that comes with REST (intent Constraints), not a policy breach.

Cache: the hyphenated symbol in _DAY_FILE is anchored by the interval and date groups, and the existing symbol == directory check stays. Neither '.' nor '/' is admitted, and day_path resolves the path under the subtree. cache_info validates a --symbol against either market when none is given. The verifier's note that cache_info validates --interval against 'spot' is harmless: 6h on futures simply lists nothing.

Proof: test.log, build.log and lint.log carry the 'deferred to the runner' first line, so they are left to the runner. The runner's record in gate-build.json, for head 4ce80ac, shows 104 passed, compileall silent and 'All checks passed!'. The suite files it lists (test_data, test_data_cache, test_data_cli, test_data_rest) are the ones the diff adds, and the source tree is unchanged since then. verifier.md exercised the changed behaviour directly: spot and futures fixtures, the high/low check, the second load with no fetch, a mid-range spot failure, the current day, the 429 reset wait and the CLI epilogs.

Tests (could they pass with the bug present?): the stub enforces the spot end-exclusive, newest-kept rule and the futures end-inclusive, oldest-kept rule, with page caps. test_page_cut_short pins the exact gap span, candle count and cached file for both markets, which kills a wrong-coverage mutant. test_page_that_does_not_move_the_window kills the missing-guard mutant. test_futures_end_of_window_row asserts on fetch_range's own frame, which kills removal of the '< end_ms' filter. test_days_fetched_before_a_download_error asserts which day files exist after the error.

Pre-existing tests: this is a feature-type change. The deleted Binance stub, the six fixtures and the Binance-only tests are declared on plan.md Proof's ratchet line, as the intent approved. The behaviours that stay (retries, gaps, cache, CLI, input checks, redirects, https-only, datetime bounds) keep tests with the same names.
Skip markers: there are no skip or xfail markers under tests/. The gate's ratchets check at build listed skip_markers: [].

Claims against today's code: the plan says read_day returns None for another schema and that the old subtree is never read; SUBTREE now equals 'kucoin', so the old subtree is never reached. The plan says no other module imports app.data; a grep over *.py finds BinanceBanError, WeightPacer, pacer_for, frame_from_rest and frame_from_csv nowhere, and the only binance/vision hits outside tests are the two permitted deprecation notes. scripts/measure_storage.py is updated to the eight columns and to validate_symbol(symbol, market). docs/decisions/index.md does not exist.

Blast radius: no guardrail file (.claude/**, CLAUDE.md, REVIEW.md, sdlc.yaml, policies/**) is in the diff. The stale CLAUDE.md lines are named for the owner in plan.md. There is no new dependency and pyproject.toml and ci.yml are unchanged. Existing Binance cache files become invisible to cache-info and cache-clear, as intended.

Policies: data-conventions rule 4 is covered by the deprecation notes (panel #1) and the schema stays defined once in schema.py. ux-and-brand: errors are one line with exit 2 and the copy lives in module constants. coding-standards: no dead Vision code remains, and the oversized test module was split by area.
Drive: commands.drive is not used; plan.md lists no drive files and there is no evidence/proof/. Not applicable.
Risk list: the delegation reported hits: {}, so no brief was written.
